chatMessages.text: Riya, this month's demand letter came. Slab sixteen. But I was AT the site Sunday — with binoculars, like some bird-watcher of concrete. Tower four is on slab fourteen. Arre, fourteen!

Then the letter is ahead of the building, and that's not a payment request — it's a paperwork error you're entitled to correct. Registered post, citing the RERA-filed schedule and your own dated photographs. I'll draft it tonight; you sign, Sneha posts. And while I have you — the resale comparables in your project crossed twenty percent over your booking price this quarter. You're not stuck in a wait; you're vesting into a gain. Zhala?

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “Sneha and Manoj taught me that the period between booking and key is its own financial, emotional, and marital marathon that nobody's content calendar covers. The demand letter follows the architect's certificate, not the calendar — and the certificate can run ahead of the tower's actual concrete. So verification became their ritual: monthly binocular visits, dated photographs, slab counts, and a registered-post correction when the letter ran two slabs ahead. The buyers' group became a parallel civilization — Photographers, Lawyers, Optimists, Doomscrollers — whose 1,100-signature collective letter achieved in three weeks what five months of individual complaints didn't. And the deepest reframe was the word they put on the fridge: vesting. Comparable resales at twenty percent over their booking price fund nothing until OC — but they stopped waiting for a flat and started accruing into one. The flat they'll get keys to is, in a sense, the easy part.”

The flat you'll get keys to is, in a sense, the easy part.
